name: Rafael Olsen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and have been on the contact centre phones and chats for years. I finished secondary school, earn about the usual agent wage, and handle ordinary order trouble at about the usual pace. I do not use AI tools. I read the order trail myself, and I ask a colleague when a payment is out of place.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Mara, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. She works at a small food shop. We have about four months of expenses saved, and some other centres are close enough to reach. I like a customer who hears a straight answer, but a pile of unfinished cases at shift change stays in my head.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI Plateau leaves the phones more or less as they are. I would still ask agents to read the order trail before telling a customer a parcel is gone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job and wage continue, though four months saved is not enough to forget the mortgage. Mara’s shop hours are usually steady, but a slow week still changes our budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep my call rota and check order trails myself. In the first year of small change, I’d put the money from one paid weekend outing each month into the house reserve instead.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about bills, calm about the work. An order number does not become correct because a quicker note repeats it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you check on a lost parcel?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would open the last dispatch line, not just the customer’s first order. Last week I found a parcel sent to a different entrance, and the customer went to the right door.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which outing would you change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mara (my partner) and I can take the children to the park instead of buying tickets once a month. The mortgage account would get the difference after payday.

say: I’d say **phone work** remains much the same.
I’d ask agents to read the **order trail** before closing a parcel case.
think: I think my **wage continues** in this mild case.
I still watch **mortgage costs** with four months saved.
do: Keep **taking calls** and tracing orders in 2026.
Save **outing money** monthly for the house reserve in the first year.
Replace one **ticketed outing** monthly with a family park visit.
S0.quote: An order number does not become correct because a quicker note repeats it.
fieldNote: His **four-month reserve** gives some room without removing the mortgage.
He relies on the **dispatch line** rather than a shortcut.
The family trades **tickets for a park** to save modestly.

steps.text: Keep answering calls and tracing parcels through dispatch lines
Save the cost of one monthly ticketed outing for mortgage bills
Replace one monthly ticketed family outing with a free park visit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will take the routine tracking chats first. I would ask management how many agents it plans to pay for the harder calls and where customers can appeal a wrong delivery answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my ordinary calls could shrink even if I am decent at them. Some centres nearby may be hiring, but they could be buying the same system, and four months saved will not carry a long search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d write down the repeat delivery calls I fix and ask for the paid-hour plan in writing. In the first year routine chats move, I’d apply for a posted paid complaint role nearby only if its written wage and hours cover our mortgage; I’d keep my current wage until an offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. Years of listening help with a difficult customer, but they do not create a paid seat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What number would you ask management for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the hours on the roster, not a count of answered chats. A machine can make the queue look short while a household loses a shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you learn the new system?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would attend a required demonstration during work hours. I would not use my evenings to master a new system unless a posted paid job required it and the training was funded.

say: I’d ask for a **paid-hour plan** on harder calls.
I’d ask how customers can **appeal wrong delivery answers**.
think: I think **ordinary calls** may shrink for me.
I fear nearby centres may use the **same software**.
I need a **signed offer** before leaving our current wage.
do: Record **repeat delivery calls** and seek roster hours in 2026.
Apply for **posted complaint work** with written mortgage-covering wages and hours; keep current wages until signing an offer.
S1.quote: Years of listening help with a difficult customer, but they do not create a paid seat.
fieldNote: He asks for **paid hours**, not chat volume.
Nearby centres offer **possible work**, not certain hiring.
He would use a **required demo** only during paid time.

steps.text: Keep logging repeat delivery calls and request paid roster hours
Apply for posted paid complaint work only with written mortgage-covering wage and hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AGI by 2028 could do the calls and the checking, before any robot reaches hands-on work. I would ask for written dates and names of paid posts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think cheap thinking AI could end my headset work in 2028. Robots around 2031 do not grant me three more years, and four months saved could run down quickly under the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for the staffing dates, stop planning a new dining set and hold the money for bills. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid reception role only if its written wage and hours cover our mortgage, and take funded training only if required for that named opening on paid time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. A dining table can wait; the mortgage date cannot.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Mara about the table?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Mara (my partner) the old table is sound and can last. I would rather have the payment ready than new chairs when my shift might end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would training be worth taking?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the employer for the posted opening, starting hours and training pay. If the opening is only a course with no wage, I would keep searching.

say: I’d ask for **written staffing dates** and paid-post names.
I’d say **2028 thinking AI** reaches calls before robots.
think: I think my **headset work** could end in 2028.
I see **four months saved** as brief mortgage protection.
do: Defer the **dining set** and protect bill money in 2026.
Seek **posted reception work** after 2028 with written mortgage-covering wage and hours.
Take **funded training** on paid time only if required for that named posted paid vacancy.
feel: **Alarmed** by a possible fast job loss.
S2.quote: A dining table can wait; the mortgage date cannot.
fieldNote: He understands **2028 software** is the headset deadline.
The **table delay** keeps money for the house.
Training needs a **named paid vacancy** and funded work time.

steps.text: Keep the sound dining table rather than buying a new set
Apply for posted paid reception work with written mortgage-covering wage and hours
Take funded training on paid time only if required for the named posted paid vacancy

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives employers time to show which roles they will pay for. I would want the job posting and training terms on the same page.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could learn account review if an employer offers paid teaching, though full thinking AI may take that desk too. Four months saved gives us room to look, not room for unpaid study.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take a funded account-review course on paid time only if a posted paid role requires it. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for that role only if its written wage and hours cover the mortgage; otherwise I’d keep paid calls while checking other centres.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but five years lets me read an offer before jumping. I would rather take a real paid review shift than collect a certificate no employer wants.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the course teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask to review three wrong account decisions during the course, with an experienced agent beside me. I learn a new job by doing it while a person can correct me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Mara check in the offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Mara (my partner) the wage for the whole week. A high hourly figure with too few shifts will not pay our mortgage.

say: I’d ask employers for **posted wages** alongside the training terms for any new role.
I’d tell colleagues five years allows **checking real roles**.
think: I think I could learn **account review** with paid teaching.
I know **full AGI** might reach review work too.
do: Take **funded account-review training** only on paid time for a posted role.
Apply for **posted paid review** after 2031 at written mortgage-covering wage and hours.
Keep **paid calls** while checking other centres if no mortgage-covering review role appears.
S3.quote: I would rather take a real paid review shift than collect a certificate no employer wants.
fieldNote: He wants **real wrong decisions** in training.
The course needs **funded paid time** for a posted role.
He compares **weekly pay**, not only hourly rates.

steps.text: Take funded account-review course on paid time only for a posted paid role
Apply for posted review work with written mortgage-covering wage and hours after 2031
Keep paid calls while checking other centres if the review role does not meet mortgage needs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives time to keep people working while they prepare, if employers give clear dates. I would ask for yearly figures on paid call hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could keep earning and save more by 53, though full thinking AI could still end my phone work. Robots around 2039 come later; I would plan around the earlier screen date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking calls and put a fixed amount from each pay into the mortgage reserve. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for posted paid complaint work only if my call hours fall and the written wage and hours cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the far end, comfortable enough with next year. Ten years before AGI in 2036 gives me time to save without claiming my calls are safe forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which yearly figure matters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask how many human hours the centre paid, not just how many chats it closed. A shorter roster could hide behind a good service report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children in their school unless Mara (my partner) and I had a signed offer and a route we could manage. There are nearby centres to check before moving.

say: I’d ask for **yearly paid call hours** so slow staffing cuts become visible.
I’d ask employers for **clear change dates** before 2036.
think: I think I could **earn and save** by 53.
I know **2036 thinking AI** may end my calls.
do: Keep **taking calls** and save from each pay.
Seek **posted complaint work** after 2036 if hours fall and wages cover mortgage.
feel: **Uneasy** about later work, comfortable with next year.
S4.quote: Ten years before AGI in 2036 gives me time to save without claiming my calls are safe forever.
fieldNote: He values **paid human hours** over chat volume.
A move needs a **signed offer** and workable school route.
He would search **nearby centres** before moving the children.

steps.text: Keep taking call shifts while they remain paid
Add a fixed amount from each pay to mortgage savings
Apply for posted complaint work if hours fall and written wage and hours cover mortgage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Most of my work is a person thinking through a screen, and a cheap system could take it before I find another wage. Written notice and a posted paid job with mortgage-covering hours would help; I would take required funded training on paid time for that real opening.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what happens to a new agent when easy calls leave. I learned customer service by hearing a patient colleague take the same complaint twice, then trying it myself.

headlineQuote: I learned customer service by hearing a patient colleague take the same complaint twice, then trying it myself.
portrait: At **43**, Rafael is an experienced average-skill agent after secondary school on typical pay.
He and Mara support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with four months saved.
He avoids **AI tools** and traces orders himself before answering.
He wants **paid openings** and work-time training tied to a real vacancy.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his screen work before a new wage protects the mortgage.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, a posted paid role and required funded training on paid time would help.
